outcome: development of endometriosis in the abdominal wall
accuracy of imaging for lesion typing
cohort: A total of 228 patients aged 32.7 +- 4.2 with abdominal wall endometriosis, who attended Changzhou Second Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from January 2013 to December 2022.
finding: BMI, number of caesarean sections, operation time, bleeding, and postoperative hospital stay were statistically significant between solitary and complex lesion groups, and latency time, CA125, maximum diameter of the lesion, operation time, bleeding, and postoperative hospital stay differed significantly among different depths of infiltration.
mod_finding: The direction of incision for caesarean section had no significant effect on the development of endometriosis in the abdominal wall or whether the lesions were multiple.
